pages.title: First steps
pages.text: When getting into $(thing)LV$(), you may feel a bit overwhelmed but wary not things are easier that you may expect. Gregtech has a lot of similarities with other tech mods.$(br2)You have generators producing power, named EU and not FE/RF, and you have machine using that energy to run.

pages.title: The Basics of EU
pages.text: The differences start with Energy Tier and Amperage. There is different tier of Energy following the tech progression of Gregtech, from LV to UHV everything in Gregtech is tied to a tier.$(br2)Then you have the Amperage, you can see it as a packet of Energy. Each Tier is a range of EU, with the minimum being the just over the tier before and the maximum being a full Amp.

pages.title: More about Tier
pages.text: If you feel a bit overwhelmed, don't worry too much for now. Just understand that your LV machines can only run LV or ULV recipes.$(br2)When browsing EMI, you will notice at the bottom right of the recipe the minimum tier required to run a recipe. LV Machines run LV or under recipe, MV Machines can run MV recipes or under, etc...

pages.title: More about Amp
pages.text: Let's go back to Amp, as we were saying 1 Amp (or 1A) is the maximum EU of a tier in one packet. So 1A LV equals 32 EU, most recipes will require on average 1A, but sometimes they will cost less so it's always useful to check the cost of your recipe.$(br2)Also know that if a machine has its Energy Buffer over 50% it will ask for 1A but whenver it goes under 50% it will ask for 2A. This will be important when we explain cables.

pages.title: Generating Power
pages.text: Initially you will have acces to three kind of generators. Each of them will only work with a specific list of fuels.$(br2)You can see their lists through EMI but we advised you to look at the Energy Chapter in the Quests to see the progression and more details for each of them.

pages.title: Moving Power
pages.text: Moving Power is a bit different. Each cables also have a Tier and will burn if transfering an higher tier. But they also have a maximum Amp capacity and will burn if carrying more. For example a 1x Tin Cable will burn if carrying more that 1A LV so if you machine asks for 2A (if under 50%) it will automatically burn the cable.

Moving energy around in GregTech can be tricky as $(thing)most cables are lossy$(). For every block, for every amp, you might lose energy as it travels through your wires. But don’t worry, there is solutions:

• Cover your wires with rubber. By doing so, you'll significantly reduce energy loss over distance.$(br2)• Use higher-tier cables. Platinum cables, for example, only lose 1 EU per block - practically nothing when compared to the 8192 EU it can carry.
